name: Mudhoney
label: Sub Pop
lede: They took their name from a Russ Meyer movie none of them had seen, put two fuzz pedals on a Sub Pop single, and were still making records for the label in their fourth decade.

eras.title: Out of Green River, into a fuzz box
eras.text: Green River broke up on Halloween 1987, and the next day Steve Turner got a call from Mark Arm about starting something dumber and louder. With ex-Melvins bassist Matt Lukin and drummer Dan Peters, they made the two Sub Pop records that put Seattle's fuzz sound on the map.

years.h: Mudhoney practice for the first time on New Year's Day
years.p: Arm and Turner, fresh out of [[Green River|78f56916-fe11-4110-8f10-d553ddf8de7b]], bring in ex-[[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] bassist Lukin and [[Bundle of Hiss|aaa673a8-af81-4140-8cb8-800406c1eace]] drummer Peters.
years.xp:
Green River had split on Halloween 1987. Turner told Rolling Stone that Arm called him the day after and said, "Hey, you should move back down here and we should start another band."

Arm's reason for leaving: he wanted to get "more grimy and punk rock" and wasn't writing any of the music in Green River.

years.h: Das Damen get an unbilled opener at the Vogue
years.p: Mudhoney's first show is at the Vogue in Seattle, with the New York band [[Das Damen|b3f7feae-06fc-4281-9919-f662c1a86287]] headlining. It comes less than four months after that first practice.

yt: Touch Me I'm Sick, Berlin, October 1988
years.h: Touch Me I'm Sick comes out on brown vinyl
years.p: Sub Pop's limited 7-inch pairs Touch Me I'm Sick with Sweet Young Thing Ain't Sweet No More, recorded with [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]].
years.xp:
Bruce Pavitt first heard Mudhoney on a boombox recording, according to Wikipedia, and sent them to Endino at Reciprocal Recording.

Arm later said the single brought both Sub Pop and the band attention and critical acclaim.

years.h: Superfuzz Bigmuff takes its name from two pedals
years.p: The six-song EP is named for the Univox Super-Fuzz and the Electro-Harmonix Big Muff, the fuzz boxes Turner and Arm played.
years.xp: [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] listed Superfuzz Bigmuff among his favorite albums in his 1993 journal. Sub Pop reissued it in 2008 as a deluxe set with the early singles, demos and 1988 live tapes.

years.h: Sonic Youth cover Mudhoney while Mudhoney cover Sonic Youth
years.p: Sub Pop's Singles Club puts both covers on one 7-inch: Sonic Youth play Touch Me I'm Sick, Mudhoney play Sonic Youth's Halloween.
years.xp:
It started when Pavitt sent Sonic Youth a short tape of early Mudhoney for feedback, and the two bands proposed covering each other.

Sonic Youth then took Mudhoney on tour through the West Coast, the Southwest and the UK. Arm has said the connection gave Mudhoney instant credibility in Britain.

eras.title: The British press gets there first
eras.text: The UK press loved Mudhoney before America noticed. A European tour opening for Sonic Youth, two Lamefests and a self-titled album got them there, and by 1991 they had the biggest-selling record Sub Pop had put out. A dispute over royalties was already building.

years.cap: Mudhoney at the Manchester International, December 1, 1989
years.h: Sonic Youth take Mudhoney to Europe
years.p: Mudhoney's first European trip is as openers for [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]]. In May they return to the UK for a show with some 150 press guests on the list.

years.h: A car antenna takes Turner's hand in Nijmegen
years.p: At a chaotic show in Nijmegen, Netherlands, Turner injures his hand on a car antenna. Mudhoney finish the tour anyway.
years.xp: Arm's own account, per the fan history: "I jumped into the crowd, threw a few drunken waterlogged punches and got back on stage."

years.big: "The definitive turning point in the Seattle music scene."
years.h: Lamefest fills the Moore Theatre with Mudhoney, Tad and Nirvana
years.p: Sub Pop co-founder Bruce Pavitt's later verdict on the night. Mudhoney top the bill at Seattle's 1,350-seat Moore Theatre, which sells out.

years.h: The first 3,000 copies of Mudhoney come with a poster
years.p: The self-titled debut album is a limited "collector's edition" on Sub Pop, with a fold-out sleeve and a poster, according to the band's fan history.

years.cap: Mudhoney at the Manchester International, December 1, 1989, two days before the Astoria
years.h: Nirvana lose a coin toss and open for Mudhoney at the Astoria
years.p: Sub Pop flies the British press to the Astoria on Charing Cross Road. [[Tad|867d3fb7-9cd1-47a4-a8f0-de29cdca2004]] and Nirvana play first; Mudhoney close the night.
years.xp: Pavitt called it Sub Pop's biggest press opportunity ever, with Mudhoney and Nirvana playing in front of the entire British music press. [[Dan Peters|3402566b-20dc-47f1-973b-2af1dedae702]] watched Nirvana fight broken strings and later admitted he'd sat there thinking the set was a disaster.

years.h: Mudhoney land in Australia for the first time
years.p: The March tour starts a long bond with the country, which later supplies their bassist [[Guy Maddison|81e68e3f-23e1-432a-bdc0-112df4ed728e]].

years.h: Nirvana borrow Dan Peters for Sliver
years.p: Between drummers, [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] and [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]] borrow Peters. He plays on the single Sliver before [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]] settles in.

years.h: Every Good Boy Deserves Fudge becomes Sub Pop's best seller
years.p: Mudhoney record it cheaply on eight tracks at [[Conrad Uno|883e716f-9299-426c-9d43-71ca6cb070ba]]'s Egg Studios in spring 1991, and the major labels come calling.

eras.title: A major label, and the backlash
eras.text: Mudhoney took a major-label deal as Seattle went global. Arm nearly died of an overdose, Kurt Cobain died, and the British press that had crowned them turned on them for still being around.

years.cap: Arm on stage at Newcastle Polytechnic, October 1992
q: The company didn't seem to give a shit or have a clue.
years.h: Mudhoney walk away from Sub Pop over royalties
years.p: Mudhoney and the label disagree over royalties and accounting on Every Good Boy Deserves Fudge. After talks with Epic fall through, they sign with Warner Bros. subsidiary Reprise.
years.xp:
According to the band's history, Arm said Sub Pop had been holding back royalties to fund other projects, and the two sides disagreed on how many copies the album had sold. He says the tension went back "since the time that the self-titled record was released."

The split didn't last forever. Mudhoney came back to Sub Pop in 2002, and Arm ended up running the label's warehouse.

years.big: "And all of a sudden, you'd go to a show and none of those people were around anymore."
years.h: Mudhoney contribute Overblown to the Singles soundtrack
years.p: Arm on the Seattle crowd, explaining the song Mudhoney wrote for Cameron Crowe's Singles.
years.xp:
Mudhoney got a $20,000 budget to record the track and spent about $164 on the actual recording, according to Songfacts, keeping the rest.

Arm's picture of the old scene: a couple hundred people who went to shows and knew each other by sight, until the boom.

years.h: The Reprise debut is named Piece of Cake
years.p: Turner explained the title as a nod to how easily things had come to Mudhoney, and later called the songs half-baked.

q: If I was alone, I would have been dead for sure.
years.h: Cobain keeps Arm alive on a hotel-room floor
years.p: On New Year's Eve, Arm overdoses on heroin in Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love's room at Seattle's Inn at the Market. Cobain and [[Supersuckers|6fa09822-bbe4-4ff8-901d-4a39a4dd82e9]] guitarist Ron Heathman take turns giving him CPR until paramedics arrive.
years.xp:
The story is in Mark Yarm's grunge oral history Everybody Loves Our Town. Arm had been at a New Year's Eve show at RKCNDY before going to the room, and he decided to use more.

Heathman recalled that Love first considered calling Sub Pop's Jonathan Poneman instead of paramedics, and that Cobain insisted on the call. Arm: "I OD'd probably five times. If I was alone, I would have been dead for sure."

years.h: Five Dollar Bob's Mock Cooter Stew, cut in 45 minutes
years.p: The band's fan history has the EP recorded on August 1, 1993, with Kurt Bloch producing, from 9:30 to 10:15 p.m.

years.h: Pearl Jam take Mudhoney to the Pacific Rim
years.p: Mudhoney spend February and March opening for [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]], which includes their old [[Green River|78f56916-fe11-4110-8f10-d553ddf8de7b]] mates [[Jeff Ament|2781b946-104c-47d3-a573-2eade82f68cd]] and [[Stone Gossard|ca7e6e03-4973-45ef-8833-98774a2d4138]].

years.h: My Brother the Cow arrives eleven months after Cobain's death
years.p: The third Reprise album gets savaged in Britain, where Turner said the press were angry Mudhoney were still around.
years.xp:
Recorded with Jack Endino at The Ranch in Seattle in October 1994. Turner, per Wikipedia: "There was a backlash after Kurt killed himself."

Not everyone agreed. People told readers to leave the brooding anthems to Pearl Jam, because Mudhoney delivered pure grunge.

years.h: Chris Farley and David Spade share a screen with Mudhoney
years.p: Mudhoney appear as the band at an MTV concert in Black Sheep, playing Poisoned Water.

years.h: Jim Dickinson takes Mudhoney into the blues on Tomorrow Hit Today
years.p: Recorded across three cities, Mudhoney's last Reprise album gets four stars from Rolling Stone. Dickinson, a Memphis producer, had worked with [[The Rolling Stones|b071f9fa-14b0-4217-8e97-eb41da73f598]].

eras.title: Lukin quits, the band doesn't
eras.text: Lukin went off to carpentry, Reprise let Mudhoney go, and for a while the band looked finished. Instead they found an Australian bassist, went home to Sub Pop and made some of their angriest records.

years.h: Lukin leaves to work as a carpenter
years.p: After a long spring world tour, Lukin says he hasn't enjoyed touring for years and his heart isn't in playing music anymore.
years.xp: Reprise ended Mudhoney's contract soon after. The three who were left had not decided whether there was a band to keep.

years.h: Mudhoney become the New Strychnines for a Sonics tribute
years.p: Arm, Turner and Peters regroup in April. As the New Strychnines, with [[Scott McCaughey|90626a1d-dd4d-41eb-ab4b-b5799a81d9a7]], they play a [[The Sonics|16346cf4-4d2b-40ec-8393-0fc7296d92fe]] tribute at the opening of the Experience Music Project.

years.h: Lukin comes back for one last run of dates
years.p: His shows run from December 2000 into January 2001, then he leaves for good.

years.h: An Australian from Lubricated Goat takes the bass
years.p: [[Guy Maddison|81e68e3f-23e1-432a-bdc0-112df4ed728e]], who played in [[Lubricated Goat|43034f79-d08f-49e3-a9f0-54b9b6a28508]] and in Arm's side band Bloodloss, becomes Mudhoney's bassist.

years.h: Home to Sub Pop with Since We've Become Translucent
years.p: The first album with Maddison, and the return to the label that started them.

years.h: Arm fills in for Rob Tyner on an MC5 tour
years.p: Arm tours with the surviving [[MC5|08b736bb-1c82-40b4-8b0b-49e2182a067a]] members, covering for their late singer.

years.h: Under a Billion Suns includes Hard-On for War
years.p: The Iraq War-era album reuses the song, first cut in 2003 for the Buddyhead compilation Gimmer Skelter. Mudhoney also curate a UK All Tomorrow's Parties that year.

years.h: Green River plays again at Sub Pop's 20th anniversary
years.p: At Marymoor Park near Seattle, Arm and Turner reunite with their old Green River bandmates, including [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]]'s [[Jeff Ament|2781b946-104c-47d3-a573-2eade82f68cd]] and [[Stone Gossard|ca7e6e03-4973-45ef-8833-98774a2d4138]].
years.xp:
It came almost 21 years after Green River's last show, opening for Jane's Addiction in Los Angeles. All six members played.

Gossard's verdict, per Rolling Stone: to "celebrate our past together was a lot of fun."

years.h: [[Tucker Martine|3faa4491-806c-4e7f-a6a5-a9e41135d088]] produces The Lucky Ones
years.p: Mudhoney cut a fast album with Martine the same year Sub Pop reissues a deluxe Superfuzz Bigmuff.

eras.title: Still here, still annoyed
eras.text: Mudhoney outlasted the scene and the major labels. They play their old records in full, open for the Pearl Jam members they started out with in Green River, and keep putting out records on Sub Pop.

years.h: Mudhoney play all of Superfuzz Bigmuff at ATP in Monticello
years.p: At All Tomorrow's Parties in New York, they play the 1988 EP from start to finish.

years.h: Arm and Turner open for their old bandmates at PJ20
years.p: Mudhoney support [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]] on the PJ20 dates, opening for Ament and Gossard, the other half of Green River.

yt: I'm Now: The Story of Mudhoney
years.h: I'm Now: The Story of Mudhoney gets a feature-length film
years.p: The documentary tells the story with the band and their Seattle peers.

years.h: Vanishing Point marks 25 years
years.p: Mudhoney's ninth studio album on Sub Pop, out in the band's 25th year.

years.h: Ten albums in, Mudhoney put out Digital Garbage
years.p: It's their fifth studio album since coming home to Sub Pop.

years.h: Plastic Eternity lands 35 years after Touch Me I'm Sick
years.p: Mudhoney's eleventh album, and their first in five years, comes out on Sub Pop.
